headline: Models encode finite resource constraints in metabolism, growth and spatial organization
label: Cellular Resource Allocation Models
summary: Predictive models now encode constraints, trade-offs and spatial heterogeneity that shape how cells partition finite resources.
synthesis: The dominant thread is mechanistic modelling of how finite cellular resources are partitioned and constrained. A genome-wide, reaction-resolved model of metabolism formalizes electron generation, transfer and disposal, and reports that carbon source sets electron flux. A mechanistic model linking ribosomal protein mass fraction, cell size and growth rate is tested against proteomes from 97 prokaryotes. A spatially resolved hybrid stochastic-deterministic reaction-diffusion model of the yeast galactose switch integrates chromosome, ER and ribosome localization. An ensemble-estimated multiscale model of EL222 optogenetic protein production in K. phaffii adds phototoxic light stress as an explicit constraint. The shared advance lies in encoding resource constraints, size limits, spatial heterogeneity and stress as explicit elements of mechanistic models.
